claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced toughness relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Solute segregation at grain boundaries primarily governs the alloy's enhanced plastic strain and toughness.
Annealing at approximately 1000°C promotes grain-boundary solute segregation in WTaTiVZr.
Rapid cooling after annealing limits excessive grain growth.
The resulting grain boundaries are enriched in Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
The multicomponent nature of WTaTiVZr facilitates segregation of reactive elements to grain boundaries during annealing.
Grain-boundary solute segregation reduces grain-boundary energy.
Grain-boundary solute segregation enhances intergranular cohesion.
Enhanced intergranular cohesion limits the formation and propagation of intergranular cracks.
Suppression of intergranular cracking enables greater plastic deformation and fracture toughness.
Annealed WTaTiVZr will exhibit less intergranular cracking than identically annealed pure tungsten.
Annealed WTaTiVZr will exhibit a higher peak plastic strain than identically annealed pure tungsten.
Annealed WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater fracture toughness than identically annealed pure tungsten.
Mechanical improvements in WTaTiVZr will correlate with grain-boundary solute enrichment measured by atom probe tomography.
Pure tungsten lacks comparable solute segregation and therefore will not show corresponding segregation-driven improvements in toughness or plastic strain.
The proposed benefit requires temperatures at which solute mobility is sufficient for segregation.
Excessive grain growth or incomplete segregation can limit the proposed mechanical benefit.
